children: Zip's U.S. app activity helps keep its bull at Citi positive on the Australia-listed installment-payment provider. Analyst Siraj Ahmed tells clients in a note that September U.S. downloads were up 11% on a year earlier, while active users grew 16%. This helps support his forecast of 35% growth in September-quarter U.S. total transaction volume. That's down from 39% in the June quarter, but Ahmed points out that Zip is up against a strong comparable period. He forecasts U.S. net bad debts of 1.78% in the September quarter, up from 1.68% three months earlier. Citi keeps a buy rating on the stock and lifts its target price 3% to 3.30 Australian dollars. Shares are up 2.4% at A$2.17. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
